summary: Monday's session is a partial rebound after Friday's tech rout (S&P 500 -1.1%, Nasdaq -2.1%, worst week since June): US index futures are up about 0.5% to 0.9%, the Kospi closed +1.8% at 5,768 while the Nikkei lost 0.6% and the Taiex 0.6%, and early Europe was down 0.8% to 1.3%. Oil fell about 2% (Brent near 107.5) after Trump put new Russia tariffs and sanctions on hold, though Brent had settled Friday at 109.86, its highest since May, with tanker attacks near Hormuz. Indonesia's market is the regional stress point: MSCI flagged a move to 'standalone' status and the index fell as much as 11% on Friday, its worst day since 1998, with Indonesian shares still volatile Monday. China reported Q3 growth of 4.5% on strong exports, and the 10-year US yield sits near 5.1%. All price tables below show Friday 2026-10-16 closes, the latest full session; Monday moves appear in notes.
